seo.title: About This Site
seo.description: How these tutorials are written, what the version numbers mean, and why every page states what was tested and when.

blocks.text: This site publishes step-by-step technical tutorials. Every guide is written against a specific software version, states that version prominently, and includes a command you can run to confirm each step produced the expected result.

Each guide is written by working through the task in a clean environment, starting from nothing. Steps are recorded as they are performed, not reconstructed afterwards from documentation. When a step fails, the failure is kept — it becomes an error entry with its own page.

The `Tested with` line on every page records the version and environment used. When a guide is re-verified against a newer release, that line is updated and the modification date changes. Guides that have not been re-verified carry their original date rather than a refreshed one.

items: Beginner — assumes you can use a terminal and edit files, nothing more.
Intermediate — assumes familiarity with the tool's basic concepts and a working project.
Advanced — assumes you can debug build output and reason about data flow without guidance.

blocks.text: If a step no longer works on the version listed, that is a bug in the guide, not a problem with your setup. Error pages accept corrections the same way guides do: the fix is tested before the page is updated.
